clinician.trajectory_summary: A 65-year-old male presented with a three-week history of red-eye and was found to have a firm, oval, dark brown, vascular, dome-shaped, non-mobile, lobulated subconjunctival mass (7×6×3.2 mm) in the right eye. Pre-operative examination revealed no intraocular extension on dilated fundoscopy or gonioscopy. The patient underwent excisional biopsy using a no-touch technique with 3 mm margins, partial sclerectomy, and cryotherapy. Intraoperatively, no intraocular extension was noted. Histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis, demonstrating large vascular channels lined by endothelial cells and filled with red blood cells separated by fibrous interstitium, with no signs of malignancy or necrosis. At six-month follow-up, the patient showed no signs of recurrence.
